title: Implement useClickOutside Detector
problemStatement: Implement `setupClickOutside(refNode, onOutsideClick)` that listens for document clicks and invokes `onOutsideClick()` only if the clicked target is outside `refNode`.
interviewTrap: Forgetting that `ref.current` can be null before mounting or after unmounting.

testCases.name: Fires callback when clicking outside referenced node
testCases.testFn: const node = document.createElement('div'); const outside = document.createElement('span'); let called = false; const listener = setupClickOutside(node, () => { called = true; }); listener({ target: outside }); return called;

testCases.name: Does NOT fire callback when clicking inside referenced node
testCases.testFn: const node = document.createElement('div'); const child = document.createElement('button'); node.appendChild(child); let called = false; const listener = setupClickOutside(node, () => { called = true; }); listener({ target: child }); return called;

testCases.name: Handles null ref gracefully
testCases.testFn: let called = false; const listener = setupClickOutside(null, () => { called = true; }); listener({ target: document.createElement('div') }); return called;

details.name: Fires callback when clicking outside referenced node

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: `useRef(initial)` returns a plain JS object `{ current: initial }` that is guaranteed to be the exact same object reference on every render. Mutating `ref.current = value` is completely synchronous and NEVER triggers a component re-render.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for DOM Node Containment via Refs.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, DOM Node Containment via Refs maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal
